_why: Round two, 11 September 2026 evening. Round one measured sixteen arms on B19's 113 pairs and its own
predictions were mostly wrong: the escape-via entry, predicted at 65 or better, came back at 54 against a
base of 54; the leg test, predicted at 60, came back at 55; turning the staircase OFF, predicted at 45 or
worse, came back at 55, one ABOVE base.
The one thing that moved was the corridor slack, and it moved in BOTH directions from the default 0.12:
0.08 gave 60 and 0.15 gave 59. A default that is beaten on both sides is not a local optimum, it is an
unlucky point, so this sweep walks the parameter properly instead of guessing a third value.
Predictions are what I actually expect after round one, not what is safe.

the best single knob of round one (60) with the slim retry that was worth +2 on its own (56 against 54); they act at different moments, so I expect them to add rather than overlap
the leg test was worth +1 alone; with the better slack I expect it to be worth no more, and this arm is here to say so rather than to win

turning the staircase off was worth +1 at the default slack, which I read as noise rather than a finding; at the better slack I expect it to be neutral or worse, and if it is better again the staircase needs a measurement of its own
more corridor-end candidates cost three pairs at the default slack (20 against 23 on the DIFF100 pass); I expect the same here, which would settle that the candidate count is not a lever
